dedupe_keys.name: hurricane interdependencies of transport and electric power in miami dade agent based model

description: This study builds an agent-based model of a Miami-Dade community to show how the electric power and transport networks depend on each other during and after a hurricane. Tasnuba Binte Jamal, Samiul Hasan and co-authors created a library of agents for power network components, road network components, wind and flood hazards and households, and applied it to ZIP code 33147 in Miami-Dade County, Florida. Interdependency is modelled in two directions: transport carries fuel to power plants and gives restoration crews access, while power outages disable traffic signals and other road components. The model was validated against Hurricane Irma (2017) data and behaved consistently across hazard intensities. Scenarios compared component-based, distance-based and traffic-light-based restoration; prioritising traffic lights restored signals quickly without delaying household power, and restoration is faster when crews are not blocked by inaccessible roads and fuel is not delayed. Coverage: one ZIP code area. Access: free arXiv preprint and the peer-reviewed article in ASCE Natural Hazards Review. Licence and cost: free to read under the arXiv non-exclusive licence; the journal version is copyrighted. Caveats: a single small area, simplified hazard fields, and no released model code was found. It informs agent-based restoration planning and cascading failure studies; it relates to the Miami-Dade evacuation centre data in the catalogue.
